ATHENS, Greece, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rubico Inc. (Nasdaq: RUBI) (the "Company," "Rubico," “we” or “us”), a global provider of shipping transportation services specializing in the ownership of vessels, today announced it has entered into a securities purchase agreement (the “Purchase Agreement”) with a single institutional investor (the “Holder”) to issue senior convertible notes (the “Notes”) in the aggregate principal amount of $9,444,444, bearing an original issue discount of 10% and warrants (the “Warrants”) to purchase common shares with an aggregate initial cash exercise price of $9,444,444. The Company expects to issue such Notes and Warrants on or about October 19, 2026 (the “First Tranche Closing”), subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. The Company will receive gross proceeds of $8,500,000 at the First Tranche Closing.

The Notes are unsecured and will bear an interest rate of 8.00% per annum if paid in cash and 10.00% per annum if paid in Common Shares. The Notes will mature 12 months after issuance, subject to extension at the Company’s option to 18 months, provided that upon such extension the principal amount of the applicable Note will be increased by 5%. The Notes will be convertible at a conversion price equal to the lower of the closing price of the Company’s common shares immediately prior to issuance or the average closing price over the five days prior to issuance (the “Fixed Conversion Price”). The Fixed Conversion Price with respect to the First Tranche Closing will be $0.3646. The Notes are also convertible at the Holder’s option at an alternate conversion price equal to the greater of 85% of the lowest daily volume-weighted average price of the Company’s common shares during the 10 trading days preceding the conversion date and a floor price of $0.10.

The warrants will be immediately exercisable, will expire on the five-year anniversary of the issuance date and will have an initial exercise price equal to the Fixed Conversion Price. At the First Tranche Closing the Company expects to issue Warrants exercisable to purchase 25,903,577 common shares at an exercise price of $0.3646 per share.

In addition, subject to certain conditions set forth in the Purchase Agreement, the Company may issue and sell to the Holder in a second closing (the “Second Tranche Closing”) an additional $5,555,556 in aggregate principal amount of the Notes and Warrants to purchase common shares with an aggregate initial cash exercise price of $5,555,556. The Company would receive gross proceeds of $5,000,000 at the Second Tranche Closing.

In addition, at each of the First Tranche Closing and the Second Tranche Closing, the Company has agreed pursuant to the Purchase Agreement to issue a number of common shares (and/or pre-funded warrants in lieu thereof) (“Commitment Shares”) to the Holder equal to 5% of the face value of the principal amount of the Notes issued at each closing divided by the Fixed Conversion Price with respect to the relevant tranche. At the First Tranche Closing the Company expects to issue 1,295,179 Commitment Shares (and/or pre-funded warrants in lieu thereof).

Maxim Group LLC is acting as the sole placement agent in connection with the offering.

The securities described above are being offered pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form F-3 (File No. 333-297207), which was declared effective by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) on July 14, 2026. A prospectus supplement relating to the securities to be issued in the Offering will be filed by the Company with the SEC. When available, copies of the prospectus supplement relating to the Offering, together with the accompanying prospectus, can be obtained at the SEC's website at www.sec.gov or by contacting Maxim Group LLC, at 300 Park Avenue, 16th Floor, New York, NY 10022, Attention: Syndicate Department, or via email at syndicate@maximgrp.com or by telephone at (212) 895-3745.

Furthermore, the Company owns three 47,499 dwt MR tanker newbuildings scheduled for delivery in the second, third and fourth quarters of 2029 and a 60-meter newbuilding megayacht scheduled for delivery in the second quarter of 2027, which the Company intends to divest.

After manufacturing, third parties added built-in cameras to the wall outlets; UL Solutions did not evaluate the modified products and recommends that they be immediately removed from service and discarded.

NORTHBROOK, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--UL Solutions (NYSE: ULS), a global leader in applied safety science, issued a public notice regarding ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) and duplex wall outlets that were UL Certified by the original manufacturer and bear the UL Mark, but were subsequently modified by third parties to include hidden cameras in the construction.

UL Solutions issued a public notice regarding ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) and duplex wall outlets that were UL Certified by the original manufacturer and bear the UL Mark, but were subsequently modified by third parties to include hidden cameras in the construction.

The GFCI and duplex wall outlets employing cameras have not been evaluated by UL Solutions and are not authorized to bear the UL Mark when they employ cameras. UL Solutions does not certify GFCI or duplex outlets that include a hidden camera.

The GFCI or duplex wall outlets covered by this notice are sold under the product names “Hidden Surveillance Camera GFCI Wall Outlet, Spy Security Camera” and “Hidden Surveillance Camera Outlet, Spy Security Camera 20 Amp” on e-commerce platforms, including Amazon, in the United States. The affected GFCI and duplex wall outlets bear a “Merlan” brand sticker and employ camera components.

It is unknown whether the GFCI and duplex wall outlets employing cameras function as intended or comply with any safety requirements. It is unknown whether the GFCI and other safety features will operate as intended to mitigate an unsafe condition. UL Solutions recommends that these products be immediately removed from service and discarded.

Images of the GFCI and duplex wall outlets are available on UL.com: https://www.ul.com/news/ul-solutions-warns-gfci-and-duplex-wall-outlets-modified-third-parties-include-built-cameras.

HOUSTON, TX / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / XCF Global, Inc. (NASDAQ:SAFX) today shared the following update with shareholders:

"We understand that the recent volatility and decline in our share price have been concerning and frustrating for our shareholders, and we take those concerns seriously. We value the confidence our shareholders have placed in XCF and believe it is important to communicate openly about the progress we are making and the priorities that continue to guide us.

Although short-term market movements are outside our control, we remain firmly focused on what we can control: executing our strategy, managing our resources responsibly, strengthening our business, and creating sustainable long-term value for our shareholders.

Over the past several months, we believe XCF has made meaningful progress in transitioning our Reno facility from development and commissioning to commercial operations. We reported more than $10 million in revenue for August and over $12 million in gross product sales (a non-GAAP financial measure) for September, with daily production reaching approximately 85,000 gallons by the end of September. These milestones reflect tangible progress in building our business and the dedication of our team. We believe this progress positions XCF to respond to continued growth in demand for renewable fuels, supported by the expansion of low-carbon fuel programs across a growing number of states.

Today, we also announced the closing of our business combination with Southern Energy Renewables and DevvStream, as we work toward advancing our broader strategy to build a diversified energy platform.

We recognize that operational progress must ultimately translate into sustainable profitability, greater financial strength, and long-term shareholder value. Our management team and Board remain focused on these priorities, including disciplined capital allocation, responsible management of our capital structure, and protection of our shareholders' long-term interests.

We know that shareholder confidence is earned through execution, transparency, and results. We are holding ourselves to that standard and intend to demonstrate our progress through measurable operating performance and clear, consistent communication.

On behalf of our management team and Board of Directors, I thank our shareholders for their continued engagement and support. We remain focused on building a stronger XCF and creating long-term value for those who have invested in our future. Our responsibility is not simply to grow the business, but to ensure that the value created by that growth benefits our shareholders over the long term."

Chris Cooper
Chief Executive Officer
XCF Global, Inc.

XCF Global, Inc. is a U.S.-based producer of renewable diesel and SAF focused on decarbonizing transportation while supporting domestic fuel supply, energy security and alternative uses for agricultural waste products. Total Equity Increases 19.2% to US$114.70 Million as Company Prioritizes Expansion Across GPU Computing and AI Model Service

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VCI Global Limited (NASDAQ: VCIG) (“VCI Global” or the “Company”), today announced its unaudited financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 (“1H2026”), as it advances its strategic transition toward AI computing, AI token services and infrastructure-related opportunities.

The first half of 2026 marked a significant transition for VCI Global following the separation and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech and other non-core businesses. The Company is now concentrating its resources and capital allocation on building AI computing capabilities, commercializing AI services and developing infrastructure opportunities across the AI value chain.

At the same time, VCI Global is pursuing complementary opportunities in renewable energy, energy storage and carbon assets as it works toward a broader infrastructure model connecting AI, computing, energy and sustainability.

  • Total equity increased 19.2% to US$114.70 million as of June 30, 2026, compared with US$96.21 million as compared to December 31, 2025.
  • Total liabilities declined 17.7% to US$17.03 million from US$20.69 million over the same period.
  • Cash and bank balances rose more than fivefold to US$5.19 million from US$0.94 million, supported by financing activities and the disposal of an investment.
  • Revenue was US$2.56 million, compared with US$18.74 million in 1H2025, reflecting the Group’s portfolio restructuring and changes in its operating profile.
  • VGAIN Compute was launched, providing customers with a platform to purchase AI tokens and access multiple supported large language models, including OpenAI GPT, Kimi, Meta Llama and Qwen.
  • Acquisition of the controlling stake in PT Fine Carbon Credit Indonesia (FCCI), an Indonesian carbon asset platform associated with approximately 241,000 hectares of forestry areas across four project sites.

“The first half of 2026 represents an important inflection point for VCI Global as we reposition the Company around AI infrastructure and scalable technology services,” said Ang Zhi Feng, Chief Financial Officer of VCI Global. “While revenue declined as a result of the transition, we ended the period with higher total equity, lower liabilities and an increased cash balance. Our priority is to manage liquidity carefully and allocate capital to initiatives with clear commercial potential as we advance our AI services and infrastructure strategy.”

REVENUE REFLECTS PORTFOLIO RESTRUCTURING

The first half of 2026 represents a fundamental change in VCI Global’s operating profile.

The Company has completed the separation and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech, and other non-core businesses, reducing exposure to businesses that were not aligned with its longer-term technology and infrastructure strategy.

Revenue for 1H2026 was US$2.56 million, compared with US$18.74 million in 1H2025. The decrease primarily reflects businesses that have since been separated or divested, along with the transition to a more focused AI infrastructure and technology operating model.

CASH POSITION AND CAPITAL ALLOCATION

The Company intends to prioritize capital deployment based on commercial demand, financing availability and project readiness, with investment priorities spanning AI Infrastructure, GPU computing and related infrastructure.

VGAIN COMPUTE: FROM AI ACCESS TO AI CONSUMPTION

VCI Global announced the launch of VGAIN Compute on October 6, 2026, through its subsidiary V Gallant Limited.

The platform enables users to purchase AI tokens to access supported large language models, including OpenAI GPT, Kimi, Meta Llama and Qwen. Announced applications include content generation, coding, research, business applications and workflow automation.

The platform introduces a customer-facing offering through which VCI Global can pursue revenue from AI services. Its token-based model provides a mechanism for charging users for access to supported AI capabilities.

The broader market opportunity is expanding as businesses move AI from experimentation into production. Gartner forecasts worldwide AI-optimised IaaS spending of US$42.3 billion in 2026, rising to US$66.1 billion in 2027. Gartner also estimates that global spending on AI inference infrastructure will reach US$23.3 billion in 2026, exceeding the US$19 billion forecast for AI model training infrastructure.

The Company’s next priorities include expanding platform usage, evaluating additional models and developing enterprise and developer applications.

DEVELOPING AN INTEGRATED POWER–AI–CARBON ECOSYSTEM

VCI Global’s longer-term infrastructure strategy extends beyond computing capacity to the resources required to support the expansion of AI infrastructure, including electricity generation, solar power, energy storage and data center operations.

The Company intends to develop an integrated infrastructure model designed to connect energy supply with computing demand, with the objective of improving power availability, supporting scalable AI computing and enhancing long-term operating efficiency.

As AI workloads become increasingly compute-intensive, access to reliable and scalable power is becoming an increasingly important consideration in the development of data center and GPU infrastructure. VCI Global believes that combining computing infrastructure with energy development can provide greater control over critical infrastructure requirements as its AI businesses expand.

LONGER-TERM OPPORTUNITIES IN ENERGY AND FOREST CONSERVATION

VCI Global announced that V Gallant had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a 70% stake in PT Fine Carbon Credit Indonesia (FCCI), a platform associated with approximately 241,000 hectares of forestry areas across four project sites in Indonesia.

The proposed acquisition provides a potential basis for developing forestry-linked carbon credit projects, subject to transaction completion and applicable technical, legal and regulatory requirements.

The voluntary carbon market offers a potential monetization route for eligible forestry projects, but credit prices vary significantly according to project type, certification standard, carbon integrity, vintage, and buyer demand.

According to Ecosystem Marketplace’s 2025 State of the Voluntary Carbon Market report, based on 2024 transactions, the average price was approximately US$14.97 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent for improved forest management credits and US$20.44 for tree-planting and restoration credits. Some premium credits may command prices above US$50, depending on their characteristics and market conditions.

COMMERCIAL PRIORITIES AND INVESTOR MILESTONES

VCI Global’s initiatives cover several potential sources of revenue, each with different development requirements.

  • AI services: VGAIN Compute provides a live platform through which the Company can pursue paid AI model access. Commercial performance can be assessed through active paying users, token consumption, revenue and service delivery costs.
  • GPU cloud services: VGAIN Cloud is intended to support demand for AI computing. Relevant milestones include infrastructure deployment, available GPU capacity, customer contracts, utilisation and revenue generated from computing services.
  • AI data center infrastructure: Galatron AI Factory’s initial planned 5MW deployment provides a defined development milestone within the broader 500MW roadmap. Progress will depend on site readiness, power availability, funding and customer demand.
  • Energy infrastructure: Potential revenue opportunities depend on the development and ownership of specific projects, available generation or storage capacity, and contracted demand.
  • Carbon assets: FCCI represents a potential forestry-linked carbon credit opportunity. Key milestones include transaction completion, project qualification, credit issuance and actual sales.

These indicators provide a clearer basis for evaluating the Company’s progress than global market growth alone.

OUTLOOK

The global expansion of AI infrastructure presents opportunities across model access, cloud computing, data center development and supporting energy infrastructure. VCI Global has announced initiatives across these areas, beginning with the launch of VGAIN Compute and extending to planned computing infrastructure and complementary asset opportunities.

The Company’s ability to benefit from these markets will depend on execution and commercial validation. Market forecasts indicate the scale of industry investment, but they do not establish VCI Global’s future revenue, market share or profitability.

VCI Global intends to progress its initiatives in phases, with the commercial outcomes of each business dependent on customer demand, operating performance, capital availability, project milestones and applicable regulatory requirements.

“Our ambition is to build an AI infrastructure business that connects customer demand, computing capacity and the energy required to support it,” said Victor Hoo, Group Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VCI Global. “VGAIN Compute provides a commercial entry point for building customer relationships and recurring usage, while our infrastructure strategy creates opportunities to participate more deeply in the AI value chain. Over the longer term, we see the potential to develop an integrated model in Asia that brings together AI computing, energy and forest conservation.”

“We intend to demonstrate the value of this transition through execution. That means growing customer usage, bringing productive computing capacity into service and converting commercial opportunities into revenue. Those are the milestones that will define the next phase of VCI Global.” He added.

Management will continue to emphasize commercial validation, disciplined capital allocation and phased execution. The pace of development and contribution from individual initiatives will depend on customer demand, funding, regulatory considerations and project milestones.

About VCI Global Limited

VCI Global Limited is transforming into an AI infrastructure and technology group focused on AI computing, GPU infrastructure and AI token services through its businesses, including V Gallant and VGAIN Compute. Following the spin-off and divestment of its capital markets consultancy, fintech and other non-core businesses, the Company is sharpening its focus on AI-driven growth while exploring complementary opportunities in renewable energy, power generation, energy storage and forest conservation, including potential carbon credit initiatives. Through these interconnected areas, VCI Global aims to build a scalable and sustainable infrastructure platform supported by disciplined capital allocation and long-term value creation.

SAN JOSE, Calif., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blaize Holdings, Inc. The outstanding shares of Series B Preferred Stock will vote together with the outstanding shares of the Company’s common stock as a single class exclusively with respect to any proposal to adopt an amendment to the Company’s certificate of incorporation to reclassify the outstanding shares of the Company’s common stock into a smaller number of shares of such common stock at a ratio specified in or determined in accordance with the terms of any such amendment (a “Reverse Stock Split Proposal”), as well as any proposal to adjourn any meeting of stockholders called for the purpose of voting on the foregoing matter (an “Adjournment Proposal”), and will not be entitled to vote on any other matter, except to the extent required under the Delaware General Corporation Law. Subject to certain limitations, each outstanding share of Series B Preferred Stock will have 1,000,000 votes per share (or 1,000 votes per one one-thousandth of a share of Series B Preferred Stock).

All shares of Series B Preferred Stock that are not present in person or by proxy at any meeting of stockholders held to vote on the above described amendment proposal as of immediately prior to the opening of the polls at such meeting will automatically be redeemed by the Company. Any outstanding shares of Series B Preferred Stock that have not been so redeemed will automatically be redeemed in whole, but not in part, at the close of business on the earlier of (i) the business day established by the Company’s Board of Directors in its sole discretion and (ii) the first business day following the date on which the Company’s stockholders approve an amendment to the Company’s certificate of incorporation to reclassify the outstanding shares of the Company’s common stock into a smaller number of shares of such common stock at a ratio specified in or determined in accordance with the terms of any such amendment.

The Company’s Board of Directors has adopted resolutions providing that the Series B Preferred Stock will be uncertificated. The certificate of designation governing Series B Preferred Stock will provide that shares of Series B Preferred Stock may not be transferred except in connection with a transfer by such holder of any shares of the Company’s common stock held by such holder. In that case, a number of one one-thousandths of a share of Series B Preferred Stock equal to the number of shares of the Company’s common stock to be transferred by such holder will be transferred to the transferee of such shares of common stock.

LONDON, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Navigator Holdings Ltd. Under the Merger Agreement, the Company will merge into the Merger Sub (the “Merger”), with Merger Sub continuing to exist as a wholly owned subsidiary of the New Parent, and each share of common stock of the Company (“Common Shares”) will be converted into one ordinary share of New Parent. As a result, the New Parent will become the publicly traded parent company of the Navigator group of companies and intends to list its ordinary shares on the NYSE under the existing “NVGS” ticker symbol.

The Merger Agreement was entered into in connection with the previously announced intention of the Company to change its corporate domicile from the Marshall Islands to England and Wales.

The change of corporate domicile is expected to bring Navigator’s corporate structure closer in line with its operating structure, with its executive office, senior management and many of its employees in the United Kingdom, along with lenders and insurers. The move is expected to give the Company the benefit of a well-developed legal and governance framework, a competitive and stable tax regime with an extensive double tax treaty network, as well as a mature and predictable tonnage tax regime for maritime businesses such as ours.

The closing of the Merger is subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, including the approval of the Merger by the affirmative vote of holders of at least a majority of the issued and outstanding Common Shares entitled to vote thereon. The Company does not expect the Merger to have a material impact on its employees, its day-to-day business and operations, or to services to its customers.

Mads Peter Zacho, Chief Executive Officer, said:

“The redomiciliation aligns the Company’s legal structure closely with where the business is managed and operated, as well as where many of our investors, lenders and insurers are based. It further supports our commitment to strong corporate governance and transparency, and provides a robust platform for future growth, investments, and strategic opportunities.”

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / Vanta Holdings Inc. (CSE:VNTA)(OTC:VNTXF)(FSE:7BC, WKN:A4205J) ("Vanta" or the "Company"), a consumer health sciences and longevity company focused on preventative wellness and healthspan extension, and parent of the Vanta premium longevity brand, announces that, further to its news releases dated May 29, 2026, and August 21, 2026, the Company has closed, effective October 15, 2026, the second tranche (the "Second Tranche") of its previously announced non-brokered private placement (the "Private Placement"), through the issuance of 210,000 units of the Company (each, a "Unit") at a price of $1.00 per Unit, for aggregate gross proceeds of $210,000. Each Unit consists of one common share in the capital of the Company (each, a "Share") and one transferable common share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder to acquire one additional Share (each, a "Warrant Share") at an exercise price of $1.25 per Warrant Share, exercisable until October 15, 2028.

The securities issued under the Private Placement will be subject to a statutory hold period expiring February 17, 2027. In connection with the closing of the Second Tranche, the Company paid aggregate cash finder's fees of $1,500 to registered dealers.

The net proceeds of the Private Placement are intended to be allocated towards the payment of outstanding and future payables and indebtedness, including amounts owing to related parties, and corporate awareness.

Together with the closing of the first tranche of the Private Placement, the Company has raised aggregate gross proceeds of C$334,579.42 through the issuance of an aggregate of 334,579 Units pursuant to the Private Placement. The Second Tranche constitutes the final tranche of the Private Placement.

Vanta has established a strategic operating framework and infrastructure relationships to support its planned U.S.-focused peptide platform. The agreement establishes a framework for coordinating compounding pharmacy relationships, peptide manufacturing and fulfillment capabilities, compliant payment processing infrastructure, and telehealth-enabled commercialization support. The planned platform complements Vanta's existing nutraceutical and premium functional hydration portfolio and forms part of its broader consumer health sciences and longevity strategy.

SAN JOSE, Calif. & TEMPE, Ariz.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Align Technology, Inc. (“Align”) (Nasdaq: ALGN), a leading global medical device company that designs, manufactures, and sells the Invisalign® System of clear aligners, welcomes the decision of the Unified Patent Court (“UPC”) finding that aligner systems incorporating Angelalign’s Torque Ridges feature infringe Align’s European Patent EP 2 237 738 B1, which relates to Align’s Power Ridge® technology.

In August 2025, Align initiated patent infringement proceedings against several companies within the Angelalign Technology, Inc. corporate group (“Angel”) (Hong Kong Stock Exchange: 6699.HK) in multiple jurisdictions, including before the UPC, which covers participating European Union member states.

On October 16, 2026, the Paris Local Division of the UPC ruled that aligner systems incorporating Angel’s Torque Ridges feature infringe Align’s patent. The Court rejected Angel’s challenges to the validity of the patent, issued an injunction requiring Angel to recall and destroy infringing products, ordered Angel to pay damages to Align, and granted Align other relief. Angel must cease offering infringing aligner systems incorporating Torque Ridges in Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovenia, and Sweden. The decision is subject to appeal.

Commenting on the UPC decision, Arthur S. Hsieh, Align Technology vice president, Deputy General Counsel, Intellectual Property & Licensing, said, “The ruling represents a significant victory for Align and underscores the importance of protecting the innovations resulting from Align’s substantial and sustained investment in research and development. Angel has sought to downplay the impact of the ruling by emphasizing that Angel recently discontinued Torque Ridges in Europe and introduced a different feature called ‘Pressure Points.’ This should not obscure the significance of the Court’s decision: Angel’s Torque Ridges were found to infringe Align’s patented technology, and Angel has publicly stated that it will comply with the Court’s ruling, which requires Angel to recall and destroy infringing products, pay damages to Align, and take other remedial actions. Similarly, Angel’s characterization of Pressure Points as an “upgrade” or “next generation” of Torque Ridges should not be understood to establish that the two technologies are technically equivalent or that Pressure Points provide an equivalent alternative to Torque Ridges. Angel’s own public materials describe Pressure Points as based on the longstanding use of “hand-made dimples” to apply targeted forces to teeth. Align does not view Angel’s Pressure Points as a technological upgrade to, or an equivalent replacement for, the ridge-based technology at issue in the UPC proceeding.”

Align’s Power Ridge® technology is designed to apply targeted forces to improve root torque control and support predictable tooth movement. The Power Ridge feature remains available as an integral part of the Invisalign® System, providing doctors with differentiated technology to support high-quality patient care.

Align has not taken a public position on whether Angel’s Pressure Points implicate Align’s intellectual property rights. Align will continue to evaluate products and technologies offered by Angel and other market participants and will take appropriate action when necessary to protect its innovations and intellectual property.

The October 16 decision follows other recent developments in Align’s global patent enforcement actions against Angel. In February 2026, the UPC issued a preliminary injunction requiring Angel to cease infringement of Align’s patented ClinCheck® Live Update technology. That decision was subsequently upheld by the UPC Court of Appeal, and proceedings on the merits remain ongoing. In July 2026, the U.S. International Trade Commission (“ITC”) conducted an evidentiary hearing concerning five patents asserted by Align against Angel. Align expects an initial determination regarding the merits of its claims in November 2026. In August 2026, the Jinan Intermediate People's Court in China issued a first-instance judgment finding that Angel's use of its MasterForce biomechanical simulation system and ATreat digital orthodontic treatment design system to generate A7 and A7 Speed premolar extraction treatment solutions infringes Align's patent rights. The court further found that aligner products manufactured and sold using the accused technology also infringe. Angel has appealed the Jinan Court’s decision. Align continues to pursue additional patent infringement actions against Angel in China.

Align remains committed to advancing orthodontic treatment through differentiated technologies backed by decades of research, engineering, clinical experience, and investment, and to vigorously protecting the intellectual property underlying those innovations.

Align’s Cutting-Edge Global Operations

As a global leader in digital orthodontics and restorative dentistry with nearly 23.5 million Invisalign® patients treated worldwide, Align continues to transform the orthodontic industry through its global operations, advanced manufacturing capabilities, and doctor-directed treatment planning. Annually, Align invests over $300M in technology to give patients of all ages access to the smiles they want and deserve through Invisalign-trained doctors.

Align’s operations span the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regions, with clinical treatment planning centers in Costa Rica, Poland, China (Chengdu), Spain, France, Germany, and Japan. The company’s global aligner manufacturing operations includes world-class facilities in Juarez, Mexico; Wroclaw, Poland; and Ziyang, China; Vienna, Austria; San Jose, CA; and a new aligner manufacturing facility coming online in 2027 in Hyderabad, India, together forming the backbone of the world’s largest 3D printing network for dental aligners (appliances).

Align’s investments in global operations are designed to bring its facilities closer to doctor-customers and their patients. In Mexico, the Juarez facility serves as a strategic node in Align’s global supply chain, enabling fast and cost-effective delivery of aligners to customers in the U.S., Canada, Latin America, and beyond. In China, the Chengdu treatment planning center and Ziyang manufacturing facility are central to Align’s long-term investment strategy for China, supporting the local economy and one of its fastest-growing markets by helping Chinese doctors provide millions of Chinese consumers access to high-quality orthodontic care. Wroclaw, Poland is the operations hub for Align’s EMEA business, bringing operations and support closer to the more than 63,000 Invisalign-trained doctors in the region.

About Align Technology, Inc.

Align Technology designs and manufactures the Invisalign® System, the most advanced clear aligner system in the world, iTero™ intraoral scanners and services, and exocad™ CAD/CAM software. These technology building blocks enable enhanced digital orthodontic and restorative workflows to improve patient outcomes and practice efficiencies for over 302.0 thousand doctor-customers and are key to accessing Align’s 600-million-consumer market opportunity worldwide. Over the past 29 years, Align has helped doctors treat approximately 23.5 million patients with the Invisalign System and is driving the evolution in digital dentistry through the Align™ Digital Platform, our integrated suite of unique, proprietary technologies and services delivered as a seamless, end-to-end solution for patients and consumers, orthodontists and GP dentists, and labs/partners. Visit www.aligntech.com for more information.

For additional information about the Invisalign system or to find an Invisalign doctor in your area, please visit www.invisalign.com. Key Terms

injunctionregulatory
A court order that tells a person or company to stop doing (or requires them to start doing) a specific action, like selling a product, closing a deal, or carrying out a transaction. For investors it matters because an injunction can pause revenue-generating activities or delay mergers and trades—like a legal “pause button” that can quickly change a company’s cash flow, risk profile, and share price while the court matter is resolved.
preliminary injunctionregulatory
A preliminary injunction is a court order that temporarily stops a party from taking certain actions while a legal case is ongoing. It’s like a warning sign that prevents someone from moving forward with plans that could cause harm or unfair advantage until the court makes a final decision. For investors, it signals that there may be unresolved legal issues affecting the parties involved, which can impact a company's operations or value.
evidentiary hearingregulatory
A hearing where a judge or administrative official allows parties to present evidence, call witnesses, and make factual arguments before making a decision. Think of it as a short, focused trial used to resolve disputed facts or decide whether certain legal or regulatory steps should proceed. Outcomes can change a company’s legal exposure, compliance status, or the timing of regulatory actions, which can affect investor expectations.
first-instance judgmentregulatory
A first-instance judgment is a court’s initial decision after a full trial or hearing, issued by the court that first hears a case rather than an appeals court. It matters to investors because it sets the first official outcome on disputes over contracts, liabilities, damages or regulatory matters—like a referee’s call in a game that can be challenged on appeal—so it can affect a company’s legal obligations, financial exposure and market perception until any appeal resolves it.
